brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut: they keep 5.9% profit vs peers' 3.8%, and their cash is stuck 25 days longer than similar firms — so offer faster payment in exchange.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price cut across rigid plastic packaging SKUs.
priceAsk.target: Target the lower end of the market band for similar items: ₹0.65–0.80/pc for caps (market typical is ₹0.85–0.95/pc).
priceAsk.basis: They keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms — that extra 2.1 points is room in their price. Market verdict says 'MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec', so the ask is grounded.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (move from 30 days to 15 days) in exchange for the price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹22.57 L of cash for us — but their cash is stuck for 104d vs peers' 79d, so quicker payment is worth roughly their borrowing rate (12.19%) to them.

brief.financialLeverage: Chemco is healthy — CRISIL A+ / Stable rating, makes good profit (5.9% vs peers' 3.8%), and they're growing fast (22.1%/yr). But their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d for similar firms, so they need cash flow. We're tiny to them (0.59% of their revenue), so we can't strong-arm, but the combo of faster payment and credible alternates gives us leverage. Lead with the trade: we pay quicker, they cut price.

evidence.point: They keep more profit than similar firms
Their cash is stuck longer than peers
Market band for a similar cap shows headroom
evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc ask, ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, verdict: modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

evidence.point: We're a small customer to them
Paying 15 days faster frees up cash for us

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue), makes pharma bottles and caps — the strongest second-source candidate, health B (65/100).

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue), serves pharma with pails and containers — robust alternate, health B (73/100).

risks: We're only 0.59% of their revenue (₹5.49 Cr spend vs ₹937.60 Cr sales), so we have limited clout — don't bluff with the alternates unless we're ready to switch.
They're in the 'grey zone' on distress risk (Altman Z 2.17) — not in trouble, but not rock-solid either. Push hard on price, but keep the tone collaborative so we don't spook a supplier we depend on.

No internal benchmark: we don't have a 'best price we pay' figure for this material, so the ask leans entirely on the market band and their profit gap — be ready to defend the ₹0.65–0.80 target with the market data.

If they refuse the trade (faster payment for lower price), we lose ₹22.57 L in freed-up cash and may have to fall back to a smaller ask or walk to an alternate — map out the switch plan before the meeting.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about aligning our price with the market and speeding up payment — you're keeping 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms, and we see room to bring our cost down while helping your cash flow.
